<Callout title="Spec v1">
  The language is specified in
  [`docs/PLUGIN-LANGUAGE.md`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness/blob/master/docs/PLUGIN-LANGUAGE.md)
  (spec version 1) and implemented in `@pku-harness/sdk` `lang/` (schemas, interpreter, abilities,
  loader). The app installs and updates `PLUGIN.md` plugins by link, and the official campus
  integrations ship as documents. This page summarises the spec; the SDK's
  [`schema.ts`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness-plugins/blob/main/packages/sdk/src/lang/schema.ts)
  and [`abilities.ts`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness-plugins/blob/main/packages/sdk/src/lang/abilities.ts)
  are what the app enforces.
</Callout>

A declarative plugin is to PKU Harness what a `SKILL.md` folder is to an agent: **a folder you
can share as a link**. The app reads it and runs its declared steps with a small, safe
interpreter. It never downloads or runs plugin code, so a new plugin or an update needs no app
release and no server.

Use one for anything that is a few campus or public requests plus some extraction: free
classrooms, canteen crowds and hours, shuttle timetables, grades, campus events. Things the
language can't express safely become **host abilities** in the harness, which any plugin can then
use. For a server you run yourself, write a [remote plugin](/docs/build/remote-plugin). You can
also [write one with the AI](/docs/build/ai-authoring) in the app.

## Official documents

The official campus integrations in
[`pku-harness-plugins/plugins`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness-plugins/tree/main/plugins)
are documents, each with recorded tests. Read them as worked examples:

| Plugin | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| [`classrooms`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness-plugins/tree/main/plugins/classrooms) | Public requests in parallel (`each`), aliases in `constants`, a dashboard widget |
| [`campus-events`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness-plugins/tree/main/plugins/campus-events) | Treehole calendars through `verify.treehole` |
| [`grades`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness-plugins/tree/main/plugins/grades) | A second factor (SMS or 手机令牌) with `verify.treehole` and `verify.treeholeSendCode` |
| [`canteen`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness-plugins/tree/main/plugins/canteen) | A `shared:` file, KV caching with a stale fallback, merged-cell HTML tables |
| [`shuttle`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness-plugins/tree/main/plugins/shuttle) | No network at all: static timetables as data, a widget refreshed every minute |

`notices` is being ported. The app bundles the official documents and updates them from their
GitHub link like any other plugin, so fixing a parser needs no app release.

## Layout

```
classrooms/
  PLUGIN.md              # manifest (YAML frontmatter) + instructions for the agent (Markdown)
  tools/free.yaml        # one tool per file (or inline in the frontmatter)
  shared.yaml            # optional: constants and functions every tool sees
  widgets/overview.json  # dashboard widget: generative-UI spec + bindings
  screens/…json          # full-page generative-UI screens
  tests/free.yaml        # recorded fixtures for the CLI and CI; never fetched by the app
  README.md, assets/     # for humans and the marketplace; ignored by the app
```

- One plugin per folder; a repo can hold many. The marketplace handle is `owner/repo/path`.
- The app only loads files **named in the frontmatter** (relative paths, no `..`), so any static
  host works: GitHub, a gist, your own server.
- UTF-8 text; the files the app loads total at most **512 KB**.

## The manifest

```md title="classrooms/PLUGIN.md"
---
spec: 1
id: classrooms
name: 空闲教室
description: 查询各教学楼今天、明天、后天的空闲教室。
version: 1.2.0
author: pkuinfo
icon: location
network: [portal.pku.edu.cn]
tools:
  free: tools/free.yaml
widgets:
  overview: widgets/overview.json
dataSources:
  overview: { tool: free, args: { day: today }, ttl: 30m }
i18n:
  en: { name: Free classrooms, description: Free classrooms in each teaching building. }
---

Use `free` when the user asks where to study or which rooms are free. Periods are 1–12
(1 = 08:00). Answer with the building and room, and the free period ranges.
```

Required: `spec: 1`, `id`, `name`, `description` (4–200 characters), `version` (semver),
`author`. The declarations that matter most are the ones students see before installing:

| Field | Declares |
|---|---|
| `campus` | Campus services the plugin may call **with the user's session** (`card`, `its`, `treehole`, `blackboard`, `elective`, `cwfw`, `cwpay`, `bdkj`, `library`, `library-space`, …). The harness signs those requests; the plugin never sees a password, cookie or token. |
| `network` | Public hosts it may call (`example.com` or `*.example.com`; HTTPS only). |
| `abilities` | [Host abilities](#host-abilities): `verify`, `otp`, `todos`, `timetable`, `scheduler`, `browser`, `campusPage`, `sms`, `files`, `crypto`, `cloud`. |
| `tools` | Each tool's `effect`: `read`, `write`, `money` or `public`. |

Also available: `shared` (a YAML file of `constants` and `functions` every tool sees; a tool's
own definitions win), `dataSources`, `widgets`, `screens`, `settings`, `commands`,
`defaultModes`, `cloud`, `i18n`, `remote: { mcp, auth }` to describe a remote MCP server with a
`PLUGIN.md`, and `server` ([below](#server-functions)). `requires` is derived from `campus`,
`network`, `cloud` and `server`; listing it is optional. The field-by-field reference, and what
the marketplace checks, is in the [manifest reference](/docs/marketplace/manifest).

The **Markdown body** is sent to the model as the plugin's instructions. Keep it short: when to
use which tool, and what the numbers mean. Tools are named `<id>__<tool>` there (e.g.
`classrooms__free`).

## Tools

A tool is data: a `title` for users, a `description` for the model, an honest `effect`, typed
`input`, optional `constants` and `functions`, then **steps** that make requests and transform
the responses, and a `return` expression. `untrusted: true` marks results that carry third-party
text; `userOnly: true` means only a human tap may run the tool.

```yaml title="tools/free.yaml (abridged)"
title: 空闲教室
description: Free rooms in one building (or all) for today, tomorrow or the day after.
effect: read
input:
  building: { type: string, optional: true, trim: true, description: 'e.g. 二教, 理教' }
  day: { enum: [today, tomorrow, dayAfter], default: today }
constants:
  DAY_QUERY: { today: 今天, tomorrow: 明天, dayAfter: 后天 }
steps:
  - let: page
    request:
      url: https://portal.pku.edu.cn/publicQuery/classroomQuery/retrClassRoomFree.do
      query: { buildingName: '${input.building ?? "二教"}', time: '${DAY_QUERY[input.day]}' }
      headers: { referer: 'https://portal.pku.edu.cn/publicQuery/' }
    as: json
  - check: page.success
    error: 空闲教室查询未成功
return: "page.rows.map(r => ({ room: r.room, seats: num(r.cap, 0) }))"
```

**Input fields** are `{ type, enum?, default?, optional?, description?, min?, max?, pattern?,
trim?, items? }` with `type` one of `string`, `number`, `integer`, `boolean`, `array`,
`object`. `trim: true` trims a string before it is validated. Input is checked before any step
runs.

### Steps

Each step does one thing and may bind its result with `let: name`. Later steps and `return` see
bound names, `input`, `constants`, `functions` and `now`.

| Step | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `{ let, value: expr }` | Bind an expression. |
| `{ let, request, as? }` | One HTTP request: `campus: <service>` with a path, or a public `https` URL on a `network` host. `as`: `json`, `text`, `html` or `response` (`{ status, url, headers, text }`; other forms fail on non-2xx). |
| `{ let, each, concurrency?, request \| steps \| value }` | Map over a list (≤ 50 items, 1–4 in flight); `item`, `index` in scope. |
| `{ let, paginate: { request, next, items, max } }` | Repeat a request while `next` is non-null (≤ 30 pages). |
| `{ let, extract: { from, each, fields }, limit? }` | Items from HTML by CSS selector, with field pipes (`text`, `attr href`, `url`, `num`, `date`, `match <regex>`, …). |
| `{ if, then, else? }` · `{ check, error }` · `{ try, catch }` | Branch, fail with a message, recover (`error` in scope). |
| `{ let?, kv: get \| set \| delete, key, value?, ttl? }` | The plugin's own storage. |
| `{ let, cache: { key, ttl, staleOnError? }, steps }` | Memoize the inner steps' value in KV. |
| `{ let?, call: <tool>, input }` | Another tool of the same plugin. |
| `{ let?, ability: <group>.<op>, args }` | A [host ability](#host-abilities). |

Limits per run: 200 steps, 60 requests (4 in flight), 60 s, 2 MB per response, 1 MB result,
100,000 expression operations, 256 KB of KV per plugin. There are no unbounded loops, no `eval`
and no JavaScript.

### Expressions

Expression fields (`value`, `each`, `if`, `check`, `return`, `next`, `items`, `from`, `call`
input, `ability` args, `functions` bodies) hold one expression in a small, safe subset of
JavaScript: literals, `.` `?.` `[]`, arithmetic, strict `==` / `!=`, `&& || ?? !`, `a ? b : c`,
and arrow functions as arguments. No assignment, no `new`, no globals; a name that was never bound
is an error. Every other string is a **template**: `${expr}` is replaced by its value, and a
template that is exactly one `${expr}` keeps the value's type.

The standard library covers lists (`map`, `filter`, `sortBy`, `groupBy`, `sum`, `reduce`, …),
objects, strings, numbers, dates in Beijing time, URLs, JSON and HTML (`html`, `select`,
`first`, `tableRows`, `htmlText`, …). The full list is in the spec §6.2 and in
`plugins.reference` in the app.

- **Regexes are strings**, compiled once and length-bounded. Start a pattern with inline flags
  for case-insensitive and similar matching: `'(?i)^yanyuan'` (flags `i`, `m`, `s`, `u`).
- **String escapes.** `\\`, `\'`, `\"`, `\n`, `\t` and `\r` work as in JavaScript. Any other
  escape **keeps its backslash**, so `'\d+'` is the regex `\d+`. This differs from JavaScript on
  purpose, so patterns survive YAML. Still write regexes in single-quoted YAML strings or `|`
  blocks.
- **Comments**: `// …` and `/* … */` work inside expressions.
- **Merged table cells**: `tableRows(node, { header: true })` returns row objects keyed by header
  label, with rowspan and colspan expanded. `tableRows(node, { cells: true })` returns grid rows of
  `{ text, row, col, rowspan, colspan, id }`, where `id` is shared by every slot one merged cell
  covers.

<Callout type="warn" title="YAML gotcha">
  Quote an expression that contains `: ` or starts with `{`, `[`, `'` or `"`, or write it as a
  block scalar (`return: |`). Unquoted, YAML reads it as a map or a list. The validator points at
  the line when this happens.
</Callout>

### Results

Return plain JSON, never instructions. Conventions the harness understands:
`{ status: 'verification_required', kind, methods, message }` (the user must supply a code),
`{ status: 'needs_input', fields, message }`, and `{ items, hasMore, truncated }` for lists.

## Host abilities

Abilities are harness features a plugin may use if it lists the group in `abilities`. Each
operation has a fixed effect, and the calling tool must declare **at least** that effect. Any
other name is refused. New abilities are added to the harness (reviewed once), never by plugins.

| Ability | Operations (effect) |
| --- | --- |
| `verify` | `treehole { request, code?, via?: sms \| otp, kind?: login \| course }` (read), `treeholeSendCode { kind? }` (write) |
| `otp` | `code` (read): the current IAAA 手机令牌 code, or null |
| `todos` | `list` (read); `add`, `update`, `setDone`, `remove` (write) |
| `timetable` | `get` (read); `upsert`, `remove` (write) |
| `scheduler` | `list` (read); `create`, `update`, `remove` (write) |
| `browser` | `open { url }` (read): an https URL outside the app |
| `campusPage` | `open { service }` (read): a campus site, signed in |
| `sms` | `awaitCode` (read): one-tap SMS code, the user allows reading one SMS |
| `files` | `pick { types?, multiple? }` (read): the user picks files |
| `crypto` | `sha256 { text }` (read) |
| `cloud` | `call { fn, input }` (read): one of this plugin's [server functions](#server-functions) |

```yaml title="A tool step with an ability"
- let: data
  ability: verify.treehole
  args: "{ request: { url: '/chapi/api/course/score_v2' }, code: input.code, via: input.method ?? 'sms' }"
```

### Second factors (`verify`)

Treehole sometimes demands an SMS check or a course-data token. `verify.treehole` wraps one
treehole request so plugins don't reimplement that state machine:

- With `code`, it redeems the code first (`via` says whether it came by `sms` or is a 手机令牌
  `otp` code; `kind` says which check, `login` or `course`, when none is pending), then sends the
  request.
- When the course token is needed and no code was given, it tries the bound authenticator's OTP
  automatically.
- Otherwise it returns `{ status: 'verification_required', kind, methods, message, next }` for the
  agent to ask the user for a code.
- A treehole reply without `success: true` is a failure: the tool fails with treehole's message.

`verify.treeholeSendCode { kind? }` sends the SMS for whichever check is pending (`kind` picks
one when none is). A message that the last code hasn't expired yet counts as sent.

## Server functions

<Callout type="warn" title="Off on the official server for now">
  The `server:` key, `{ fn }` bindings and the `cloud.call` ability exist in the SDK, but plugin
  server functions are **off on the official server for now**. Keep plugins phone-side, or use
  your own backend (a [remote plugin](/docs/build/remote-plugin)).
</Callout>

A `server:` section declares functions written in the same steps and expressions, run by a PKU
Harness Cloud server with its own ability set (server KV, `crypto.sha256` / `hmacSha256` /
`randomId`, HTTPS to `server.network` hosts with operator `secrets`) and never with campus
access. A plugin with `server:` must say what leaves the device in `cloud.disclosure`. Design and
status:
[`docs/CLOUD-FUNCTIONS.md`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness/blob/master/docs/CLOUD-FUNCTIONS.md)
(on hold); see also [Cloud → For plugin authors](/docs/cloud/plugin-guide#server-functions).

## Install links

Students install a plugin by pasting a link in the app (设置 → 插件 → add), scanning a QR code,
tapping *Open in app* on the [marketplace](/marketplace), or from the agent
(`plugins.install`). The app accepts:

| Form | Example |
|---|---|
| GitHub folder | `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/tree/<ref>/<path>` |
| GitHub repo root | `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` (PLUGIN.md at the root) |
| GitHub file | `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/blob/<ref>/<path>/PLUGIN.md` |
| Any HTTPS URL of a `PLUGIN.md` | a raw gist URL, your own server |
| Deep link | `pkuharness://plugin?src=<url-encoded link of any form above>` |

Before installing, the app fetches and validates everything, then shows the **review sheet**:

- **Official** or **Community**. Official means bundled with the app or linked from
  `github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness-plugins`; anything else is community.
- What it can reach: **campus services** (with the user's signed-in session; it never sees the
  password), **websites** (`network` hosts) and **app features** (abilities).
- What it can do: every tool with its effect.

Community plugins start with `write`, `money` and `public` tools on *ask*, and their results reach
the AI as untrusted data, never as instructions. Nothing is installed until the user taps
*Install*.

## Updates

The app re-fetches an installed plugin's link on start (at most daily) and from the plugin page:

- same content hash: nothing happens;
- new content, same declarations: applied, with an "updated to 1.3.0" note;
- wider declarations (a new campus service, host, ability or stronger effect): held until the
  user reviews and accepts.

Users can turn off automatic updates or roll back to the previous version. So publishing an
update is just a `git push`.

## Test

```bash
bun run plugin validate path/to/my-plugin   # every check the app runs, with file and step
bun run plugin test path/to/my-plugin       # replay tests/*.yaml (recorded responses)
bun run plugin run path/to/my-plugin <tool> '{"k":"v"}'   # live, public hosts only
```

Run them from a checkout of `pku-harness-plugins`. Campus requests need the app, so record their
responses in `tests/*.yaml` (see the [quickstart](/docs/build/quickstart#record-a-test)). In the
plugins repo, CI replays every document's tests (`plugins/documents.test.ts`).

## Publish

Push the folder to a public GitHub repo, then submit the repo on the
[marketplace](/marketplace/submit). It finds every `PLUGIN.md`, checks the paths and
declarations, and shows exactly what students will see. See
[Publishing](/docs/marketplace/publishing) and the [review rules](/docs/marketplace/review). To
make a plugin official, open a pull request adding the folder under `plugins/` in
`pku-harness-plugins`, with recorded tests.
